## Overview This PR fuses FP8 KV cache writes and query quantization into Beam's QK-norm/RoPE kernel, replacing three separate kernels (QK-norm/RoPE, `scaled_fp8_quant` on Q, and `reshape_and_cache_flash`) with one for both the target model and DFlash2 drafter. **Duplicates**: No open PR does this. #63510 keeps the BF16-only insert. #57682, #38621 and #59035 are compile-time fusion passes for models built from vLLM’s standard norm/RoPE/cache ops, which Beam’s custom kernel doesn’t go through. **AI assistance**: Claude is used throughout development, and I reviewed every line of code. ## Claims - Decode step time drops on `Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4` with an FP8 KV cache: - TP4 + DFlash2: 3.8% at concurrency 1, 1.6% at concurrency 64. - TP4 w/o spec decode: 5.5% at concurrency 1, 2.4% at concurrency 64. - Outputs are numerically identical: - The fused kernel writes the same FP8 bytes as the separate quant and cache-insert kernels it replaces. - Greedy outputs are token-identical to main. - GSM8K and the spec-decode acceptance length are unchanged. ## Validation All runs on B200s, comparing main with this PR. - **Unit tests:** `pytest tests/models/test_beam_numerics.py tests/models/test_beam_construction.py` passed. The kernel tests capture the fused call in a CUDA graph and require FP8 Q and the whole cache to match `scaled_fp8_quant` and `reshape_and_cache_flash` byte-wise, including NaN and inf/-inf. - **Correctness (TP4):** - Greedy outputs on 16 prompts are token-identical to main with an FP8 cache, a BF16 cache, and `--enforce-eager`. - GSM8K 5-shot (vLLM's `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions) goes from 0.939 to 0.937 (± 0.007), and the acceptance length from 5.50 to 5.50. - **Sync and JIT checks:** with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, an eager FP8 + DFlash2 server ran with no syncs. - **Performance:** Median ITL from `vllm bench serve` (ISL=8192 / OSL=512, 1024 prompts per concurrency, `--max-concurrency c`) reduces comparing to `main` (w/o fusion). With spec decode, acceptance is fixed to 3.0 so both builds do the same work per step. | Concurrency (c) | TP4 + DFlash2 | TP4 w/o spec-decode | |---:|---:|---:| | 1 | −3.8% | −5.5% | | 4 | −2.9% | −4.7% | | 16 | −1.1% | −3.4% | | 32 | −1.4% | −3.1% | | 64 | −1.6% | −2.4% |
Full numbers and commands Each cell is one run of 1024 prompts. Throughput is output tokens/s per GPU. - TP4 + DFlash2: | c | main median ITL (ms) | PR (ms) | Δ | main tok/s/GPU | PR | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 6.275 | 6.037 | −3.8% | 106.3 | 110.0 | +3.5% | | 4 | 9.123 | 8.858 | −2.9% | 260.9 | 267.7 | +2.6% | | 16 | 13.425 | 13.281 | −1.1% | 543.0 | 549.5 | +1.2% | | 32 | 16.451 | 16.229 | −1.4% | 719.2 | 728.2 | +1.2% | | 64 | 20.327 | 20.001 | −1.6% | 891.5 | 903.2 | +1.3% | - TP4 w/o spec-decode: | c | main median ITL (ms) | PR (ms) | Δ | main tok/s/GPU | PR | Δ | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 3.842 | 3.629 | −5.5% | 61.1 | 64.5 | +5.5% | | 4 | 4.599 | 4.381 | −4.7% | 186.4 | 194.9 | +4.5% | | 16 | 6.252 | 6.039 | −3.4% | 440.0 | 452.5 | +2.8% | | 32 | 7.895 | 7.650 | −3.1% | 595.9 | 609.7 | +2.3% | | 64 | 9.715 | 9.484 | −2.4% | 772.9 | 786.8 | +1.8% | Prefill (TP4 + DFlash2, 64 uncached 8192-token prompts) moves from 86.3k to 87.4k input tok/s (+1.2%, p = 0.07), which is within noise. **Commands**: ``` vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser beam --reasoning-parser beam \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN"}' vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 0 \ --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --num-prompts 1024 --max-concurrency $c --seed $((1001 + 100 * c)) \ --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 ```
## Details - **Kernel**: New `constexpr` flags (`FP8_Q`, `FP8_KV`) add FP8 stores; the BF16 path is unchanged. To match the replaced ops byte for byte: - K is rounded to BF16 first, as main stores it before the cache insert. - K/V use `div_rn(x, scale)`, then a NaN-preserving clamp to 448/-448. - Q uses `x * div_rn(1, q_scale)` with `scaled_fp8_quant`'s clamp order. - Scales are read on device, so CUDA graphs need no host sync. - **When it fuses**: A BF16 cache, or an `fp8`/`fp8_e4m3` cache with per-tensor scales. Per-head scales and `fp8_e5m2` keep the existing path. Backend checks are unchanged. ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
